speaker: Unknown
en: Good afternoon.
zh: 下午好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope you're all having a lovely day here at AIE.
zh: 希望大家在 AIE 现场都度过了美好的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had great weather, though the UV's been like nine, so hopefully you put your sunscreen on, you're being appropriate adults.
zh: 天气一直很好,不过紫外线指数大概到了九,所以希望大家涂了防晒霜,表现得像个负责任的成年人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here to talk to you about context engineering, and I have the good fortune of following AJ from LinkedIn, because he talked a lot about the system that we actually design and sell to other solutions, and I'm gonna give you a bunch of open source tools, so if you watched that last talk just before me, you're gonna get a bunch of tool chains so you can go mess around yourself, and I'll teach you a bunch of techniques today.
zh: 我今天要跟大家聊聊上下文工程,我有幸排在 LinkedIn 的 AJ 之后演讲,因为他讲了很多我们实际设计并销售给其他解决方案的系统,而我会给你们一堆开源工具,所以如果你听了我之前那场演讲,你会拿到一堆工具链,可以自己去折腾,今天我还会教你们一堆技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal, of course, is to fix, you're absolutely right.
zh: 当然,目标是修好——你说得完全对。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they've taken that out of the prompts now, so it just says you're right or other things, but I'm sure you've all been there.
zh: 我想他们现在已经把那个从提示词里去掉了,所以现在只说“你说得对”之类的话,但我相信大家都经历过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm Brandon.
zh: 我是 Brandon。

speaker: Unknown
en: I work at Unblocked.
zh: 我在 Unblocked 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, I have a coconut.
zh: 是的,我手里有一个椰子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been giving these away for fresh context, fresh coconuts.
zh: 我们一直在送这些,为了新鲜上下文,新鲜椰子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the thing that I want to talk to you about is with these models, especially with mythoclass models, I think Fable 5's coming back today, so they say, you can watch my grain call recording, try to book this.
zh: 但我想跟你们聊的是,有了这些模型,尤其是 with mythoclass models,我想 Fable 5 今天要回归了,所以他们说,你可以看我的 grain call 录音,试着预订这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll ignore it.
zh: 我们会忽略它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what I want you to do is to think about the fact that with these tools, AI-generated code should feel like it was written by someone who's been on your team for years.
zh: 好吧,我想让你们思考的是,有了这些工具,AI 生成的代码应该让人感觉是那种已经在你团队待了多年的人写出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to get in the right headspace, for years you have to consider that you have been the context engine.
zh: 所以要进入正确的思维状态——待了多年,你必须意识到,你一直是那个上下文引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you do that?
zh: 你是怎么做到的?

speaker: Unknown
en: You built context by going to work and asking questions,
zh: 你通过去上班、问问题来构建上下文,

speaker: Unknown
en: Shipping PRs and getting them rejected, going to meetings, and all this slowly over time built up the engine that is your brain.
zh: 提交 PR 然后被拒绝,去开会,这一切随着时间慢慢累积,构建出了你的大脑这个引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: You understand how it works here.
zh: 你理解这里是如何运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know how stuff gets shipped.
zh: 你知道东西是怎么发布出去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were on call that night when you took prod down and why that happened.
zh: 你还记得那天晚上你值班把生产环境搞挂了,以及那是怎么发生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is that these agents have this exact same problem.
zh: 问题是,这些智能体面临着完全相同的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time you create a new terminal session with an agent in it, it's very intelligent, but it doesn't have any context on how your company operates.
zh: 每次你创建一个带有智能体的新终端会话,它非常聪明,但它对你公司如何运作没有任何上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it needs to get that somehow.
zh: 所以它需要以某种方式获取这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is as you move these agents up in scale, that cost compounds if you get it incorrect at the beginning.
zh: 问题在于,当你把这些智能体的规模往上扩时,如果一开始就搞错了,那个成本会不断复利累积。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll leverage off context and content.
zh: 它们会依赖上下文和内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just gonna fix this because I think people want to take some photos.
zh: 我们把这个修一下,因为我想有人想拍点照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfect.
zh: 完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: That context issue will compound.
zh: 那个上下文问题会不断复利累积。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at the far left, we all remember the age-old time of two years ago where we had tab-complete models that were pretty cool.
zh: 在最左边,我们都记得两年前那段古老时光,那时我们有了相当酷的 tab 补全模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened is it popped up and said, hey, do you want to tab this?
zh: 发生的事情是,它弹出来问,嘿,你想 tab 这个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And quickly in your head, with your context, and you go, no, that's bad.
zh: 你脑子里带着你的上下文快速判断,然后说,不,这不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you went, oh, sweet, you hit tab, nice.
zh: 或者你说,哦,不错,你按下 tab,挺好。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we move along the agentic kind of adoption curve, what happens is you are moving into more situations in which you have agents running without a human in the loop, or at least you wish you didn't have to be in the loop.
zh: 随着我们沿着智能体式采用曲线往前走,你会越来越多地进入这样的情形:智能体在没有人在环的情况下运行,或者至少你希望自己不必在环里。

speaker: Unknown
en: What they need is some way to be able to ask the questions they need when they hit walls in order to write code or solve or basically fix the issue and ultimately output code that's mergeable into your code base, especially with many people here who actually work in brownfield code bases that have been around for a long time that run real revenue across them, not just greenfield fund projects.
zh: 它们需要的是某种方式,在撞墙的时候能够提出它们需要的问题,以便编写代码或解决、基本上修复问题,并最终输出可以合并进你代码库的代码,尤其是这里有很多人实际工作在那种存在了很久、承载着真实营收的老旧(brownfield)代码库里,而不只是绿地试验项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that cost of bad context compounding at the beginning is cheap.
zh: 所以糟糕上下文在初期累积的成本是便宜的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think like shift left, finding a defect or a bug, you'll want to find it as early as possible.
zh: 如果你按“左移”的思路想,发现一个缺陷或 bug,你会想尽可能早地发现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the same with context.
zh: 上下文也是一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because as you move across, you get into doom loops.
zh: 因为随着你往前走,你会进入厄运循环(doom loops)。

speaker: Unknown
en: You usually ask your agent to do something.
zh: 你通常让你的智能体做某件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, hey, I did it.
zh: 它说,嘿,我做完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, no, man.
zh: 而你说,不,哥们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you correct and correct and correct.
zh: 然后你纠正、纠正、再纠正。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's wasted search tokens.
zh: 那是浪费的搜索 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also wasted rework time.
zh: 也是浪费的返工时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is not acceptable with the tokenomics we have coming.
zh: 而以我们即将迎来的 token 经济学来看,这是不可接受的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as you move into parallel agents, et cetera, you start hitting a review tax.
zh: 然后当你进入并行智能体等等阶段,你开始碰到审查税。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these AI code reviewers we're trying to use, but again, key context is important there so that those code reviews are able to basically understand how the operations of the business are so it knows the business logic and more.
zh: 我们正在尝试使用这些 AI 代码审查器,但同样,关键上下文在那里很重要,这样那些代码审查才能基本理解业务的运作方式,从而知道业务逻辑等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, if your hope is to move all the way out of the loop, you're like background agents, get it done, make no mistakes, you really need to make sure that you have a context engine so those agents can query it and get all the answers they need so they can keep operating in an effective way.
zh: 最后,如果你的希望是完全走出这个环,你会说后台智能体,把它搞定,别犯错,那你真的需要确保你有一个上下文引擎,让那些智能体可以查询它并获得它们需要的所有答案,以便它们能持续以高效的方式运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are some common approaches that don't work.
zh: 有一些行不通的常见做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're basically like a local maxima.
zh: 它们基本上像是局部最优。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two of the ones we see the most with our hundreds of enterprise clients and mid-market sized businesses is the curated context trap.
zh: 从我们数百个企业客户和中型企业客户来看,最常见的问题之一就是「精选上下文陷阱」。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've ever sat down and taken a virtual file system or maybe a local file system, you put some markdown files in it and you're like, here's all the context of this project, it's how it works.
zh: 如果你曾经坐下来,弄一个虚拟文件系统或者本地文件系统,往里面放一些 markdown 文件,然后说,这里就是这个项目的全部上下文,它就是这么运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You then allow your agent to grep over that and it gets a bunch of good data and then it will perform better.
zh: 然后你允许你的智能体在上面 grep,它会拿到一堆好数据,然后表现会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The issue is first now you have to distribute that so maybe throw it up in the GitHub and your team can grab it.
zh: 问题首先是现在你得分发它,也许扔到 GitHub 上让你的团队去拿。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then the next is that repo is gonna rot just like all the other docs you wrote down and then who at your org is the omnipotent one who has the taste to curate this file or repo for literally everyone in the org.
zh: 但接下来就是那个仓库会像你写过的所有其他文档一样腐化,而且你们组织里谁是那个无所不能的人,有品位为整个组织的每一个人去策划这个文件或仓库。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you start to hit these issues.
zh: 所以你开始碰到这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next is the MCP plateau.
zh: 下一个是 MCP 平台期。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one is pretty clear.
zh: 这个很清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have MCPs.
zh: 我们有 MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're great.
zh: 它们很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can give it to your agent, and now it can basically get information from another source system.
zh: 你可以把它给你的智能体,现在它基本上可以从另一个源系统获取信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is, of course, based on how you write the server description, the tool descriptions, your agent may never call it, even though it should have.
zh: 问题是,当然,取决于你怎么写服务描述、工具描述,你的智能体可能永远不会调用它,即便它本应调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if it does, there's a known bias called the satisfaction of search bias.
zh: 或者如果它调用了,有一个已知的偏差叫「搜索满足偏差」。

speaker: Unknown
en: What that means is the agent, when it finds the first piece of information that it thinks is correct, it goes, oh, I have what I need, and it proceeds.
zh: 意思是,当智能体找到它认为正确的第一份信息时,它会说,哦,我有了我需要的东西,然后继续进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: In most organizations, there's a Slack conversation from last night that says you should be doing A instead of doing B, and the agent will never find it if it found some architecture record first.
zh: 在大多数组织中,会有一个昨晚的 Slack 对话说你应该做 A 而不是做 B,而如果智能体先找到了某份架构记录,它永远不会再发现那条信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it doesn't actually consider all of the context.
zh: 所以它实际上并没有考虑全部上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem here is access to information is not understanding.
zh: 这里的问题在于,获取信息不等于理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to deliver understanding to a model, you have to do other techniques.
zh: 所以要向模型交付理解,你必须用其他技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm basically trying to say is what your agent can't see is everything below the waterline.
zh: 我基本上想说的是,你的智能体看不到的是水面以下的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can 100% get code that compiles, but that code that compiles is taking down prod and you have a P0 at 1 in the morning because it missed the fact that you have a certain rollout procedure, you're supposed to turn off a feature flag, whatever it might be.
zh: 它完全能拿到能编译的代码,但那段能编译的代码正在搞垮生产环境,你在凌晨一点有一个 P0,因为它漏掉了你有一个特定的发布流程,你应该关掉某个 feature flag,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: So your team needs a context engine because what it should do is understand who you are and where you work in an organization.
zh: 所以你的团队需要一个上下文引擎,因为它应该做的是理解你是谁、你在组织中在哪里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if I say to you, I want to get auth stood up, it knows where I work, it knows where my git commits are, it knows who reviews those commits, and it understands that my context, it can focus me and then use that as a trigger point to find the rest of the information.
zh: 所以如果我对你说,我想把 auth 搭起来,它知道我在哪里工作,它知道我的 git 提交在哪里,它知道谁审查这些提交,它理解我的上下文,它可以聚焦我,然后把那作为触发点去找其余的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It resolves conflicts, as mentioned, an old architecture diagram and last night's Slack convo with the CTO.
zh: 它解决冲突,如前所述,一份旧的架构图和昨晚与 CTO 的 Slack 对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which one is right?
zh: 哪一个是对的?

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to use a bunch of techniques to determine that.
zh: 你需要用一堆技术来判定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Respects, permissions, and governance, of course.
zh: 当然还有尊重权限和治理。

speaker: Unknown
en: MCP allows us to use OAuth and other scopes and SSO, but if someone asks a question over here who's not supposed to know about secret project A, you need to make sure that doesn't leak into the response.
zh: MCP 允许我们使用 OAuth 和其他 scope 以及 SSO,但如果这边有人问了一个不应该知道机密项目 A 的问题,你需要确保它不会泄漏进响应里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, deliver the right context at the right time to the model in a token-optimized way.
zh: 最后,以 token 优化的方式,在正确的时机向模型交付正确的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have multiple surface areas because human engineers still talk to Unblocked all the time to get information they need in Slack or otherwise, but then you want token-optimized responses if you're just speaking machine to machine in order to not waste a bunch of bold classes on your token spend.
zh: 我们有多个表面,因为人类工程师仍然经常和 Unblocked 交谈,在 Slack 或其他地方获取他们需要的信息,但如果你只是机器对机器地对话,你需要 token 优化的响应,以免在你的 token 花费上浪费一大堆 bold classes。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how an engine works.
zh: 这就是这个引擎如何运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna be brief on this, but basically on the left-hand side, you see all the data sources that are coming in.
zh: 我会简短一点,基本上在左手边,你看到所有进来的数据源。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, we focus on engineering teams, and that's who uses us, as well as the technically-like teams around it, like support, sales, and otherwise.
zh: 对我们来说,我们专注于工程团队,那是使用我们的群体,还有它周围偏技术的团队,比如支持、销售等。

speaker: Unknown
en: You ingest all that data.
zh: 你摄取所有那些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get real-time data from tools like your instant management tool chain.
zh: 你从工具那里获得实时数据,比如你的即时管理工具链。

speaker: Unknown
en: It comes into the engine.
zh: 它进入引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where that engine is, it thinks.
zh: 引擎在那里,它思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the bottom, I'll expand on that slide in a moment.
zh: 在底部,我稍后会展开那页幻灯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: But basically, it uses these six key characteristics.
zh: 但基本上,它使用这六个关键特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on the right, you output the context to the exact workflow in the manner that it is needed.
zh: 然后在右边,你以它所需要的方式,把上下文输出到确切的工作流中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those six key points, as mentioned, unified system context, you have to go across the whole thing.
zh: 这六个关键点,如前所述,统一系统上下文,你必须贯穿全局。

speaker: Unknown
en: At large orgs, companies like LinkedIn Scale, Workday, General Motors, whatever, they need this type of data, they need to understand everything that's happening, and Tharik this morning actually talking about Fable coming out potentially later today,
zh: 在大型组织,像 LinkedIn 规模、Workday、通用汽车这样的公司,他们需要这种类型的数据,他们需要理解正在发生的一切,而 Tharik 今天早上实际上谈到了 Fable 可能在今天晚些时候发布,

speaker: Unknown
en: He mentioned that you need to actually provide a map and then let Fable discover the territory.
zh: 他提到你实际上需要提供一张地图,然后让 Fable 去发现疆域。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way to help confine that is making sure that these models have access to all of the context because they will find your unknown unknowns.
zh: 帮助限定这一点的方法是确保这些模型能访问全部上下文,因为它们会找到你的未知的未知。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are definitely things going on in your company that you're just unaware of but would be really helpful for the task you're trying to do.
zh: 你的公司里肯定有一些事情你完全不知道,但对你正在尝试做的任务会非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: That'll move faster, but the targeted retrieval, you should be able to, if you provide a link quickly, unfurl it, get that document back and move along.
zh: 这会走得更快,但还有定向检索,如果你提供了一个链接,你应该能快速展开它,取回那份文档然后继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: So two tasks, deep research, go long, that's fine, but you also need speed when speed is required.
zh: 所以两种任务,深度研究,走长线,那没问题,但在需要速度的时候你也需要速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Conflict resolution, we already talked about that, but one thing says do A, one thing says do B, who is right?
zh: 冲突解决,我们已经谈过了,一个东西说做 A,一个东西说做 B,谁是对的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Personalized relevance, who am I, where do I work, what am I working on?
zh: 个性化相关性,我是谁,我在哪里工作,我在做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: That token optimization, making sure the response is good and effective and doesn't bloat the window.
zh: 还有那个 token 优化,确保响应是好的、有效的,不会撑爆窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then permission enforcement, of course, OAuth, you shouldn't see it, you shouldn't see it.
zh: 还有权限强制执行,当然,OAuth,你不该看到它,你不该看到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we did with some tests is we actually ran the exact same prompt to the same model, and one with context and one without.
zh: 我们在一些测试中所做的是,我们实际上向同一个模型运行完全相同的提示词,一个带上下文,一个不带。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the wall clock time savings, and then two hours, which was great, and then the tokens savings.
zh: 这是实际耗时上的节省,然后是两个小时,这很棒,然后是 token 的节省。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a sizable task, it took about 21 million tokens without, and then 18, or sorry, 10.8 million tokens with it.
zh: 所以这是一个相当大的任务,不带上下文用了大约 2100 万 token,然后带上下文用了 1800 万,不对,抱歉,是 1080 万 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the type of experience that you typically see when you're using a context engine because the majority of those wasted search tokens where it has to grep at the beginning of every session to understand and discover things are no longer there when it's hydrated with context.
zh: 这就是你在使用上下文引擎时通常会看到的那种体验,因为那些被浪费的搜索 token——每次会话开头它必须用 grep 去理解和发现东西——在注入了上下文之后就不再存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hydrated.
zh: 注入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as you move forward, you get these types of outcomes.
zh: 然后随着你往前推进,你会得到这类结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: 50% fewer tokens, faster triage, and the answer quality is actually better because it knew what was going on inside of the business.
zh: token 减少 50%,分诊更快,而且答案质量实际上更好,因为它知道业务内部正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now this next part
zh: 现在这个下一部分

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll probably want a photo.
zh: 你们可能想拍张照。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't know, you can actually take a picture of a QR code and then later in photos tap on it and then load the link so you don't need to float here because I'm going to give you three QR codes.
zh: 如果你们不知道,你其实可以拍一张二维码的照片,然后稍后在照片应用里点它并加载链接,所以你不需要挤到前面来,因为我要给你们三个二维码。

speaker: Unknown
en: This first one is for the social comment network.
